decision_text:
# Initial optimization decision

Minimize a deterministic scalar objective on 10 coordinates in [-5, 5]. A point is feasible only when all three returned inequalities are <= 1e-10. The hard total budget is 2000 joint objective/constraint evaluations; infeasible points and repeats count. There are no prior observations. The objective and constraints are sealed black boxes; no smoothness, feasibility volume, or location of an optimum is assumed.

## First block only
Use the provided SobolSearch wrapper (src/optimizers/sobol_search.py), backed by SciPy 1.17.1 scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol. Evaluate the box centre first, followed by 64 scrambled Sobol points across the full bounds. Set seed=20261022 and scramble=True. Inherit SciPy 1.17.1 defaults bits=None (30 effective bits) and optimization=None. NumPy is 2.4.6. The wrapper retains its sampler and observations; constraint values are retained separately by the campaign driver, and feasible selection uses the actual returned inequalities.

The maximum is 65 additional objective calls, pausing at cumulative count 65. Sixty-four Sobol points form a balanced power-of-two design; together with the centre this gives a modest initial view of feasibility and objective scales in ten dimensions, without assuming a particular function structure. No replication is required because the interface states determinism.

At the checkpoint, inspect feasibility count, observed objective range and quantiles, best feasible observation, smallest constraint violations, and which constraints are restrictive. These observations will inform a fresh decision about search method and its settings. Pause sooner on an evaluator error or nonfinite output; do not retry an unknown evaluation. Every call will be tagged sobol_initial. No subsequent optimization block is selected here.

## Decision after evaluation 65
**Budget:** 65 used / 2000 total; 1935 remaining.
**Evidence:** Five of 65 observations are feasible. Best feasible y=5676.529840299591 at evaluation 12; the next best is 5686.537395212375 at evaluation 47. Objective range is [3279.12422322939, 38719.513139606635]. The centre has y=3279.12422322939 but violates constraint 2 by 11242.920724032272. Individual feasibility counts are [51,18,59], so constraint 2 is particularly restrictive. Smoothness has not yet been established.
**Decision:** Switch from global Sobol sampling to a constrained SLSQP local trial, initialized at the best feasible point (evaluation 12). Retain all real observations, exact observation cache, Sobol state and the same harness. The local solver is new and will remain alive across a checkpoint if unfinished.
**Hyperparameters:** SciPy 1.17.1 minimize(method='SLSQP') through a campaign-local adapter. Normalize x to z=x/5 in [-1,1]^10. Divide objective by 10000.0; divide constraints by initial median absolute magnitudes [56835.00859228337, 17070.96146676898, 22529.626188712256]. Use shared forward finite differences with step 1e-6 in z (5e-6 in physical x), switching sign at upper bounds. Constraint margin is 1e-7 in scaled units, ftol=1e-10, maxiter=500, disp=False. Jacobians are supplied explicitly. Other solver internals inherit SciPy 1.17.1 defaults. Exact cached points incur no new evaluation and are not added to the trace. Scaling prevents raw constraint magnitudes from dominating numerical conditioning; the small interior margin protects feasibility near convergence.
**Reason:** A feasible starting point exists and the deterministic interface permits economical shared objective/constraint finite differences. Local differentiability is a working assumption to test, not a known property. The objective spread and tight constraint justify a constrained local method before spending more calls on broad sampling.
**Next step limit:** 220 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 285.
**Why this length:** Approximately twenty 10-dimensional gradient/step cycles provide evidence about local progress and feasibility while leaving most of the budget available. The cap counts every real probe and line-search point.
**Review:** Inspect best feasible reduction, accepted iterates, violations, line-search behavior, and numerical stability. Pause sooner on solver termination or an evaluator/nonfinite error. No next method is selected in advance.

## Decision after evaluation 285
**Budget:** 285 used / 2000 total; 1715 remaining.
**Evidence:** The 220-call local block produced 135 feasible observations and 19 SLSQP iterations. Best feasible y fell from 5676.529840299591 to 1827.219606547961 (67.81% reduction), at evaluation 275. The latest accepted iterates decreased from 1829.4753668027322 through 1828.397054248319 to 1827.219606547961. Their constraints 1 and 2 sit at the specified interior margins (approximately -0.0056835 and -0.0017071); constraint 3 retains slack near -7281. The last iteration improved by 0.06358. Finite-difference probes sometimes cross a constraint, as expected, but accepted steps are feasible. The solver is unfinished and has no error.
**Decision:** Continue the same SLSQP instance, preserving its curvature approximation, current iteration, pending request, observation cache, and single harness.
**Hyperparameters:** Retain the full configuration from the decision after evaluation 65, including finite-difference step 1e-6, scaled margin 1e-7, and ftol=1e-10. The stable feasible trajectory supports retaining scaling and derivative settings; ordinary SLSQP internal adaptation continues.
**Reason:** Strong improvement and consistent small recent decreases support finishing this local trajectory. A short near-plateau is not evidence that the method is unsuitable, and solver state remains valuable.
**Next step limit:** 110 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 395.
**Why this length:** Roughly ten further gradient/step cycles should distinguish convergence from continued local improvement. This shorter block reflects the smaller recent changes.
**Review:** Inspect solver termination, feasible incumbent reduction, step sizes and boundary behavior. Pause sooner on solver termination or evaluator/nonfinite error; choose subsequent work only after this evidence.

## Decision after evaluation 395
**Budget:** 395 used / 2000 total; 1605 remaining.
**Evidence:** The 110-call block added ten SLSQP iterations and 21 feasible observations. The incumbent improved by 0.067280448516 from 1827.219606547961 to 1827.152326099445. The most recent accepted-step reduction is 0.000034801159; two active constraints remain at the prescribed interior margin, with no numerical error. The solver is still running, and the final ten-dimensional derivative stencil is nearly complete.
**Decision:** Continue the same live SLSQP solver for a short convergence check. Preserve all state and observations.
**Hyperparameters:** Unchanged from the decision after evaluation 65. The finite-difference step and stopping tolerance remain appropriate for assessing whether this trajectory has reached its numerical stopping point; do not discard the accumulated curvature approximation for a parameter change.
**Reason:** The diminishing reductions suggest local convergence but do not establish it. A small extension is justified to obtain termination evidence at low cost.
**Next step limit:** 44 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 439.
**Why this length:** About four gradient/step cycles are enough to test the observed convergence trend without a long allocation to marginal refinement.
**Review:** Inspect termination status, final feasible objective, and constraint residuals. Pause sooner on solver termination or evaluator/nonfinite error. No future block is selected.

## Decision after evaluation 429
**Budget:** 429 used / 2000 total; 1571 remaining.
**Evidence:** SLSQP terminated successfully after 32 iterations, causing an early checkpoint after 34 of the authorized 44 calls. Best feasible y=1827.1523018054072 at evaluation 422, only 0.000024294038 below the prior block's best. Its constraints are [-0.005683499727503261,-0.0017070963831447017,-7252.16872516808]. The solver's returned objective is 1827.1523020918912; the best observed feasible value is retained instead. One converged trajectory does not establish global optimality. The initial design contains another geographically distinct feasible point at evaluation 47 with y=5686.537395212375, almost equal to the first start's original value.
**Decision:** Restart constrained SLSQP from the actual observation at evaluation 47. Preserve the first solver and all observations/cache in memory, reset only the new solver's curvature/iteration state, and retain the same harness and counter.
**Hyperparameters:** Use the same SciPy 1.17.1 SLSQP configuration documented after evaluation 65 (including scales, step=1e-6, margin=1e-7, ftol=1e-10). The first trajectory was stable, so changing initialization while holding numerical settings fixed provides an interpretable check of basin dependence.
**Reason:** A second promising but distant feasible start probes whether the converged local result depends on initialization. It has comparable initial objective quality and avoids spending extra calls merely finding a new feasible seed.
**Next step limit:** 231 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 660.
**Why this length:** Roughly 21 gradient/step cycles should reveal the trajectory and basin; the first run achieved nearly all of its reduction by iteration 19. Leave room for reassessment before deciding whether this new run merits convergence refinement.
**Review:** Compare the trajectory's best feasible objective and position with the first local solution, constraint activity and recent progress. Pause sooner on solver termination or evaluator/nonfinite error. No later restart or method is selected.

## Decision after evaluation 660
**Budget:** 660 used / 2000 total; 1340 remaining.
**Evidence:** The second local run made 20 iterations using 231 calls, including 140 feasible observations. Its latest feasible y=1827.2727908228824 remains 0.120489017475 above the incumbent 1827.1523018054072. Its latest x is Euclidean distance 0.191309 from the incumbent, suggesting attraction to the same region, but the latest decrease is still 0.124952. The run is unfinished. Data-only diagnostics trained affine constraint models on the first 48 observations and checked the remaining 612: maximum absolute residuals [3.30681e-10,9.39480e-11,8.45830e-11]. A 66-coefficient quadratic objective fit on 80 selected observations had held-out RMSE 27172.0 on 37 points and condition number 120153, so it is not a reliable objective surrogate. Model predictions are diagnostic only, never trace observations.
**Decision:** Continue the second SLSQP instance with its complete state retained. Preserve the fitted constraint models for analysis, but do not change this running solver.
**Hyperparameters:** Unchanged configuration from the decision after evaluation 65. Stable constraints and ongoing accepted-step reductions support the existing step and scaling. The poor global objective fit does not contradict local finite-difference utility.
**Reason:** This run is near the first solution but not yet locally settled. A short extension can clarify whether initialization changes the attainable objective without prematurely calling the solutions identical.
**Next step limit:** 88 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 748.
**Why this length:** About eight gradient/step cycles should resolve the current 0.12 objective gap; this is shorter than the preceding block because the trajectory has already reached the incumbent's neighborhood.
**Review:** Compare feasible value and distance to the incumbent, local convergence and constraint activity. Pause sooner on solver termination or evaluator/nonfinite error. Reconsider use of the constraint model only after the new observations.

## Decision after evaluation 748
**Budget:** 748 used / 2000 total; 1252 remaining.
**Evidence:** The second SLSQP run has completed 28 iterations. Its best recent accepted y=1827.1546882468617 is 0.002386441455 above the global incumbent 1827.1523018054072; the last improvement is 0.001496327341. The new block had 16 feasible observations among 88 calls. Both trajectories approach the same region with constraints 1 and 2 active. The first run's termination included a line search with changes near 1e-7 in raw objective, suggesting that a different local curvature model is worth checking. Data-only affine constraint fits were highly accurate, but the objective quadratic fit over broad and poorly conditioned data was unreliable.
**Decision:** Suspend the unfinished second SLSQP instance with its pending request intact; preserve both SLSQP solvers and every observation. Start a new COBYQA local trial from the best actually observed feasible point (evaluation 422). Continue the same harness. Use actual joint objective/constraint observations through a shared cache; no surrogate prediction is recorded or substituted for a real observation.
**Hyperparameters:** SciPy 1.17.1 minimize(method='COBYQA') and NonlinearConstraint, with the existing z=x/5 normalization and objective/constraint scales. Set initial_tr_radius=0.05 in z (0.25 physical), final_tr_radius=1e-7 in z, feasibility_tol=1e-12, maxfev=2000, maxiter=10000, f_target=-inf, scale=False, disp=False. Use a smaller scaled interior margin of 1e-9 (versus 1e-7 for SLSQP) to reduce conservative boundary bias while retaining a margin 1000 times the solver feasibility tolerance. Other algorithmic internals inherit SciPy 1.17.1 COBYQA defaults. Reinitialize interpolation geometry; reuse exact observations if requested again.
**Reason:** A derivative-free constrained trust-region method can learn curvature from moderate displacements and test whether finite-difference conditioning limited local accuracy. The small initial radius focuses this experiment on the known promising region; all actual returned constraints still determine the campaign incumbent.
**Next step limit:** 160 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 908.
**Why this length:** Ten dimensions require an initial interpolation design; 160 calls allow that design plus a meaningful sequence of model updates and radius adjustments before committing more budget.
**Review:** Assess actual feasible improvement, constraint margins, model progress and solver status. Pause sooner on solver termination or evaluator/nonfinite error. Any continued refinement or broader exploration will be chosen from the next observations.

## Decision after evaluation 908
**Budget:** 908 used / 2000 total; 1092 remaining.
**Evidence:** COBYQA used 160 new calls, with 89 feasible observations, and improved the incumbent from 1827.1523018054072 to 1827.1522243737056. The last five sampled feasible points each improved the objective, with the latest decrease 0.000001589403. Their constraints 1 and 2 remain near [-5.68350e-5,-1.70709e-5] and constraint 3 near -7251.2. The gain is small and partly attributable to the reduced interior margin, so this does not establish a materially different basin. The solver is unfinished and error-free.
**Decision:** Continue the live COBYQA instance, preserving its interpolation model, trust-region state, pending request and observation cache. Both SLSQP states remain stored.
**Hyperparameters:** Unchanged from the decision after evaluation 748. Recent consistent improvements favor retaining model state and the existing final radius instead of restarting to tune parameters.
**Reason:** The independent local method has found feasible improvement and is still making consistent progress. A modest continuation tests whether its evolving curvature model produces additional useful refinement.
**Next step limit:** 80 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 988.
**Why this length:** Eighty model updates are enough to assess the small but consistent recent trend, while halving the prior block length because gains are now marginal.
**Review:** Assess cumulative feasible gain, trend in recent improvements and solver termination. Pause sooner on solver termination or evaluator/nonfinite error. No further work is preselected.

## Decision after evaluation 988
**Budget:** 988 used / 2000 total; 1012 remaining.
**Evidence:** Eighty further COBYQA calls yielded 54 feasible observations and improved y from 1827.1522243737056 to 1827.152173748828, a gain of 0.000050624878. The latest evaluations differ by around 1e-7 or less. Both SLSQP starts and COBYQA have concentrated around the same location, while broad feasible coverage is still only five initial Sobol observations. Affine constraint models trained on 48 initial points previously predicted 612 held-out observations to at most 3.31e-10 absolute error. This supports using those models for candidate construction, but it does not establish objective behavior away from the incumbent.
**Decision:** Suspend COBYQA with all model and trust-region state preserved. Switch this block to constraint-guided projected Sobol sampling over the full box: continue the original sampler with its next 64 points and project each onto the affine model's feasible polytope. Evaluate every resulting candidate with the real harness, retaining actual feasibility as the selection rule. All previous solver states, observations, and the one harness persist.
**Hyperparameters:** Existing SobolSearch/SciPy 1.17.1 sampler, seed=20261022 and scramble=True, continuing from 64 to 128 total Sobol proposals. Euclidean projections are computed in z=x/5 by SciPy 1.17.1 SLSQP with analytic distance gradient and affine constraint Jacobian, ftol=1e-12, maxiter=200, and bounds [-1,1]. Use the affine models trained on the initial 48 points and a raw constraint interior margin of 1e-4, safely larger than observed model residuals. Projection is an internal distance minimization with no black-box evaluations. Other projection solver internals inherit SciPy 1.17.1 defaults. This is a boundary-biased design, not a claim of uniform sampling in the feasible polytope.
**Reason:** Local refinements now yield marginal gains, while global basin uncertainty remains. Projection makes broad exploration useful despite the initial 5/65 feasibility rate. It also probes other parts of the feasible set without imposing the incumbent's two active constraints as equalities.
**Next step limit:** 64 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 1052.
**Why this length:** The next power-of-two Sobol increment provides a reproducible broad batch at modest cost. It is enough to identify promising feasible starts or large model residuals without committing to a large global search.
**Review:** Inspect actual feasibility, best new candidate, diversity, distance to incumbent, objective distribution, and affine model residuals. Pause sooner if a projection fails, any actual point is infeasible, maximum raw constraint prediction error exceeds 1e-5, or evaluator/nonfinite error occurs. Subsequent optimization will be decided only afterward.

## Decision after evaluation 1052
**Budget:** 1052 used / 2000 total; 948 remaining.
**Evidence:** All 64 projected Sobol candidates were actually feasible; maximum raw affine constraint prediction errors were [3.47427e-10,9.14042e-11,9.09495e-11]. Their objectives ranged from 3005.9306479113275 to 58557.741764892184. The best new point (evaluation 1002) has objective 3005.9306479113275, constraints [-15827.432921357431,-9.999999747378752e-5,-4540.067479646629], and Euclidean distance 9.1230 from the incumbent. It is worse than the incumbent but substantially better than the initial values of either previous local start. Global incumbent remains 1827.152173748828.
**Decision:** Start a third constrained SLSQP run from the best actual projected observation, evaluation 1002. Reset only this new solver's curvature/iteration state. Keep the two previous SLSQP states, COBYQA state, all observations and exact cache, the advanced Sobol sequence, and the same harness.
**Hyperparameters:** SciPy 1.17.1 LocalSolver configuration as documented after evaluation 65: z=x/5, fscale=10000, original gscale, shared forward difference step=1e-6, ftol=1e-10, maxiter=500, disp=False. Change scaled interior margin to 1e-9, matching the stable COBYQA boundary margin; this reduces conservative bias and remains well above the observed numerical residuals. Jacobians still use actual joint observations, not predicted objective values.
**Reason:** Broad sampling produced a relatively low-value feasible seed far from the known solution. Descending from that seed tests basin dependence more effectively than additional unstructured samples, while the new start's lower objective merits a shorter initial trial.
**Next step limit:** 198 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 1250.
**Why this length:** Approximately eighteen gradient/step cycles should show whether this higher-quality distant seed leads to the same region or a better basin. This cap is shorter than the second start's first block because its initial value is much lower.
**Review:** Inspect feasible progress, current distance and objective gap to the incumbent, solver status, and effects of the tighter interior margin. Pause sooner on solver termination or evaluator/nonfinite error. No continuation is predetermined.

## Decision after evaluation 1250
**Budget:** 1250 used / 2000 total; 750 remaining.
**Evidence:** The third SLSQP start made 17 iterations over 198 calls, with 140 feasible observations. Its best actual feasible observation is y=1827.613196623794 at evaluation 1245, down from 3005.9306479113275. The recent reported iterates are in the same region as the incumbent, with constraints 1 and 2 close to the smaller interior margin and constraint 3 safely negative. The global incumbent remains 1827.152173748828. The third trajectory is still making substantial reductions relative to its remaining local gap and has not terminated.
**Decision:** Continue the third SLSQP instance with all its curvature, line-search state and pending request intact. Preserve every other solver and all observations under the same harness.
**Hyperparameters:** Unchanged from the decision after evaluation 1052, including margin=1e-9. The tighter margin has been numerically stable; there is no evidence requiring a different derivative step or scaling.
**Reason:** The distant, improved seed is descending successfully and is now near the known region. Finishing more of this trajectory will clarify whether it reaches a distinct value; interrupting it now would leave that test unresolved.
**Next step limit:** 132 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 1382.
**Why this length:** About twelve gradient/step cycles should resolve much of the remaining sub-unit objective gap. Earlier runs needed roughly thirty iterations to approach local stationarity.
**Review:** Inspect local value, distance to the best region, recent decrease and convergence status. Pause sooner on solver termination or evaluator/nonfinite error. No subsequent method is committed.

## Decision after evaluation 1382
**Budget:** 1382 used / 2000 total; 618 remaining.
**Evidence:** The third run completed 29 iterations and generated 29 feasible observations in the 132-call block. It improved the campaign incumbent from 1827.152173748828 to 1827.1521095674502 at evaluation 1382. The new coordinates differ modestly from earlier solutions while objective differences are tiny, suggesting weak curvature in some directions. Constraints remain feasible at [-5.6833259932886904e-5,-1.707150720875461e-5,-7419.492388518642]. Several recent line-search trial values exceeded the current best, but the latest actual observation improved it. The solver has not terminated.
**Decision:** Continue the same third SLSQP instance briefly, preserving all line-search and curvature state, all observations and the same harness.
**Hyperparameters:** Unchanged from the decision after evaluation 1052. This short check avoids discarding an in-progress line search merely to change derivative settings; reported feasibility remains numerically stable.
**Reason:** The third run has produced a small new incumbent and is close to the iteration count at which the first run stopped. A bounded convergence check should clarify its numerical endpoint before selecting a further experiment.
**Next step limit:** 44 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 1426.
**Why this length:** At most four gradient/step cycles are sufficient for this narrow question and constrain spending on marginal refinement.
**Review:** Inspect termination, final feasible value, and size of any further improvement. Pause sooner on solver termination or evaluator/nonfinite error. No next method is preselected.

## Decision after evaluation 1390
**Budget:** 1390 used / 2000 total; 610 remaining.
**Evidence:** The third SLSQP run terminated successfully after 29 iterations and only eight of the 44 authorized new calls. The best actual feasible y=1827.1521085913269 occurs at evaluation 1383. The solver returns a slightly worse point, so the trace incumbent is retained. Three local trajectories and broad feasible sampling support this region, but small coordinate shifts can change the objective at the 1e-4 level. Two constraints are consistently active; constraint 3 retains about 7423 raw units of slack. Affine constraint predictions have held to about 3.5e-10 on broad actual probes.
**Decision:** Start one active-face symmetric quadratic-model trial from the incumbent. Keep all prior solver states and observations. Project the base onto model constraints 1 and 2 at raw value -1e-6, then use an orthonormal null-space basis for the eight directions preserving those two constraints. This restriction is a local modeling assumption supported by observed activity, not a claim about the global solution. Evaluate the full symmetric stencil and one bounded regularized Newton trial through the same harness.
**Hyperparameters:** Campaign-local implementation using NumPy 2.4.6 eigh/lstsq and SciPy 1.17.1 null_space with its default SVD rank tolerance. Physical-coordinate symmetric step delta=0.002. Use 1 base point, 16 single-axis probes, 56 paired symmetric probes, and 1 trial. Build central gradient and Hessian estimates; floor eigenvalues at max(1e-6,1e-8*largest absolute eigenvalue) before inversion. Cap the trial Euclidean norm at 0.25 physical units and halve only if modeled constraints or box bounds require it. Raw active-constraint margin=1e-6 exceeds observed model residuals by more than three orders of magnitude. No library optimizer defaults apply to the explicit trial rule.
**Reason:** Small-step first-order termination may be affected by weak curvature. Symmetric probes on the supported active face directly measure curvature while keeping all measurements feasible, and a modest step cap limits extrapolation. The symmetric stencil avoids the first-order truncation bias of the earlier forward differences.
**Next step limit:** 74 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 1464.
**Why this length:** Exactly one eight-dimensional symmetric quadratic stencil plus one real trial is needed to test the curvature hypothesis and model's improvement prediction. There is no automatic second iteration.
**Review:** Inspect gradient norm, Hessian spectrum, predicted versus actual trial reduction, feasibility and constraint-model residuals. Pause sooner if a candidate exceeds bounds, any actual probe is infeasible, model residual exceeds 1e-5, or evaluator/nonfinite error occurs. Select further work only after reviewing these measurements.

## Decision after evaluation 1464
**Budget:** 1464 used / 2000 total; 536 remaining.
**Evidence:** All 74 active-face observations were feasible; maximum affine model residual was 2.62e-10. Moving the base to the smaller interior margin improved the incumbent slightly to 1827.1521080307352. The symmetric model had gradient norm 0.0697941 and Hessian eigenvalues from -1535.10 to 34109.02. Its regularized step was clipped from norm 43.55 to 0.25; predicted decrease 47.9755 was contradicted by an actual increase of 2.34078 to y=1829.4928907068115. Thus this quadratic model is not reliable at the 0.25 trial scale. Negative fitted curvature is not yet evidence of a useful descent direction. No inferior point replaced the incumbent.
**Decision:** Replace the single quadratic trial with a bounded multiscale directional scan anchored at the measured feasible base. Retain the face basis and measured Hessian/gradient. Probe both signs of the minimum-eigenvalue direction and the normalized negative-gradient direction, across seven small physical step lengths. All evaluations use the real harness and actual constraints.
**Hyperparameters:** Campaign-local deterministic scan: radii [0.002,0.001,0.0005,0.0002,0.0001,0.00002,0.000005], two unit directions in the eight-dimensional face basis, both signs. Keep the same affine constraint model and raw active margin 1e-6. Use NumPy 2.4.6 eigh for the direction. No optimizer defaults apply. These radii stay at or below the former single-axis stencil scale, avoiding the failed large extrapolation.
**Reason:** Direct observed line profiles can distinguish usable local descent from a misleading fitted negative eigenvalue, and reveal a scale for trustworthy local modeling more cheaply than immediately rebuilding a full Hessian.
**Next step limit:** 28 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 1492.
**Why this length:** Two directions times seven scales times two signs completely specifies the diagnostic scan. No subsequent local model is launched automatically.
**Review:** Compare actual objective changes, scale-dependent central slopes and curvatures, best observed feasible value and constraint residuals. Pause sooner on actual infeasibility, a raw model residual above 1e-5, bounds violation or evaluator/nonfinite error. Decide further work from this evidence.

## Decision after evaluation 1492
**Budget:** 1492 used / 2000 total; 508 remaining.
**Evidence:** All 28 directional probes were feasible. The best value improved to 1827.1520999280224 at evaluation 1469, a decrease of 8.102713e-6 from the prior base, with a 0.0005 step along the model's minimum-eigenvalue direction. Direct central curvature in that direction is positive and stable, about 50.03, contradicting the model eigenvalue -1535.10. Central slopes stabilize near -0.028864 and -0.046245 along the two tested directions as radii shrink to 2e-5 and 5e-6. Thus the broad finite-difference Hessian had serious truncation error; the failed large trial did not reveal useful negative curvature. The actual observed values, not model predictions, established the improvement.
**Decision:** Rebuild one symmetric active-face quadratic model at the new best observed point, using much smaller probes, then evaluate one bounded trial. Retain the same face construction, all previous measurements/models and solver states, and the same harness. Recompute curvature rather than reuse the unreliable large-stencil Hessian.
**Hyperparameters:** Same explicit method and library versions as after evaluation 1390, changing delta from 0.002 to 0.00002 physical units, and trust-radius cap from 0.25 to 0.002. Keep raw active margin=1e-6 and eigenvalue floor max(1e-6,1e-8*largest absolute eigenvalue). The new delta is supported by stable small-scale directional estimates; the trial cap is at the largest directly tested local scale and is 125 times smaller than the failed trial.
**Reason:** Small-scale data show smooth, positive directional curvature and a usable descent direction. A more accurate full local model can account for coupling across all eight feasible directions, while the smaller cap controls extrapolation.
**Next step limit:** 74 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 1566.
**Why this length:** One full symmetric stencil plus one real trial permits a direct comparison with the failed model, without committing to repeated Hessian rebuilds.
**Review:** Compare Hessian spectrum, gradient, actual/predicted improvement ratio and feasibility. Pause sooner under the same bounds, model-residual, actual-feasibility or evaluator-error conditions documented after evaluation 1390. Subsequent steps depend on the result.

## Decision after evaluation 1566
**Budget:** 1566 used / 2000 total; 434 remaining.
**Evidence:** The smaller symmetric stencil and trial were all feasible. Its Hessian is positive definite, with eigenvalues [0.08212,1.03631,1.30863,2.09145,7.02303,49.30624,759.13782,38115.61560], a condition ratio about 464000. The capped 0.002 trial predicted a decrease of 3.25661225e-5 and actually decreased by 3.29004888e-5 (ratio 1.0103), improving the incumbent to 1827.1520670275336. The unconstrained model step norm was 0.00779, so the successful trial was limited by its cap. The previous broad stencil's negative curvature was not reproduced at a reliable small scale.
**Decision:** Continue local active-face optimization using the validated fine Hessian as initial curvature and the actual successful trial as the current point. Use central gradient evaluations with a damped BFGS Hessian update and adaptive trust radius. Retain the fine model's base/basis and previous base gradient, all collected data and other solver states; preserve the same harness. The new live worker retains its gradient stencil and trust state if the block stops mid-iteration.
**Hyperparameters:** Campaign-local NumPy 2.4.6 trust-region adapter. Central gradient step=2e-5 physical units; initial radius=0.004 (twice the successful capped step), maximum radius=0.05, minimum radius=1e-7. Regularized Newton directions are norm-capped; accept only actual positive decrease with actual/predicted ratio>0.1. Shrink radius by 0.25 if ratio<0.25; double it when ratio>0.75 and step norm exceeds 0.8 of radius. Use Powell damping threshold 0.2 for BFGS and the same eigenvalue floor max(1e-6,1e-8*largest absolute eigenvalue). Stop internally at gradient norm<1e-7, radius<1e-7, predicted decrease<1e-14, or 1000 internal iterations. Raw face margin remains 1e-6. Bounds and remaining modeled inequalities constrain proposals, with actual feasibility/model residual checked on every observation. These are explicit adapter settings, not inherited optimizer defaults.
**Reason:** The fine model accurately predicted a real improvement and exposed severe anisotropy. Reusing that curvature with cheaper 16-call central gradients should exploit this information more efficiently than repeated 73-call Hessian stencils, while actual/predicted agreement controls extrapolation.
**Next step limit:** 102 additional objective calls; pause at cumulative evaluation 1668.
**Why this length:** About six gradient-and-trial cycles can test both the initial curvature and the BFGS updates. Rejected trials cost one extra call and also count toward this cap.
**Review:** Inspect feasible incumbent improvement, model agreement, accepted/rejected trials, radius adaptation and termination. Pause sooner on solver termination, model/feasibility failure, bounds violation or evaluator/nonfinite error. Decide later work only after the checkpoint.

## Decision after evaluation 1668
**Budget:** 1668 used / 2000 total; 332 remaining.
**Evidence:** The trust-region block used 102 calls, all feasible, and accepted all six trials. Best y improved from 1827.1520670275336 to 1827.1519746612814, a decrease of 9.23662522e-5. Gradient norm fell from 0.05727 on the first update to 0.002709 before the last trial. The last actual reduction was 5.46333e-7 with actual/predicted ratio 0.2464, triggering the configured radius contraction from 0.008 to 0.002. Earlier ratios were 0.681 to 1.593. The solver is unfinished and error-free.
